This game has potential, but I find myself too needled by annoyances to say I recommend it. The whole game has a clunky unwieldy feel to it. Load times are long, menus on controller use a cursor which feels sluggish, gameplay is a spectacle but feels lacking. After playing it for a bit I find myself wanting to play Darktide instead for a better experience. Why do I feel more in control with a reject than a space marine? At least they fixed the disconnects.

This game is a breath of fresh air. Ignore all the "game review" sites as their criticisms aren't valid since they do not understand the lore of the game and the universe of Warhammer. While everything is inherently political, the politics being brought into discussion by these "game review" sites ignore the context behind the game and most of these points they bring up is irrelevant or not productive. If they want female space marines, we have the sisters of battle. They can turn to that as a lore-accurate close alternative to female space marines.

It's a breath of fresh air because it's a fun game to play that is not filled to the brim with micro transactions or a live service model into it.

In terms of the story, I find it interesting and cool. I'm new to the Warhammer universe and ever since I started to play this game, I started to get balls deep into the lore and can't stop.

To conclude, this game is fun and can't wait to see what else the studio behind this game does.

I was recommended Space Marine 2 by a friend, and as my first Warhammer game, I have to say it did not disappoint.

After a hefty load time and an unskippable intro that initially sparked nostalgia, I was ready to dive in. The game is visually stunning, with satisfying gunplay and solid melee combat that makes every encounter feel epic. In my opinion, Space Marine 2 stands out in a landscape where many AAA titles struggle with both graphics and storytelling. While the story itself isn’t groundbreaking, it has a captivating feel that drew me in, making me want to learn more about the world, despite it not being all that interesting to me. Plus, they just let me play—none of the cutscenes have been painfully long—cough cough Final Fantasy XV cough cough.

While I found the campaign to be short and somewhat average, I still think it’s worth playing for the sheer fun of it. I appreciate that the PvP feels less about having the fastest PC or spamming buttons, and more about outsmarting opponents using knowledge of mechanics and class limits. It’s refreshing to see a game that rewards strategy over "brute force"—looking at you, Street Fighter V.

The co-op operations are enjoyable and replayable thanks to the different classes, although I agree we need more content and maps to keep things fresh.

Overall, I find Space Marine 2 to be an exhilarating experience, even if it can get a bit repetitive. It’s a solid addition to any co-op game collection and is highly recommended, whether you’re a 40K fan or not. It’s no wonder the Steam reviews have been extremely positive, especially considering how games that cost more than $10 are under heavy scrutiny.

End Review

On a separate note, I think more unique looks for characters would be awesome—something like how it was back in Halo 3 with the Hayabusa helmet. It was completely different, but everyone wanted it and, low key, respected it to some degree.
